verdict_reason: all frozen criteria met on MPS

gate_scope_statement.what_the_gates_measure: The three reprojection-derived gates -- flip control, per-hand span ratio and wrist anchor registration -- measure WIRING correctness: whether the left-hand mirror is undone, whether the predicted hand is at the right scale, and whether the MANO+camera projection lands on the reference anchor. A broken mirror, a 2x scale slip or a wrong crop centre would pass every accuracy number in this file while corrupting everything downstream, so these are what is gated.
gate_scope_statement.what_they_are_not: These thresholds were calibrated on this run. They are NOT an accuracy claim about HaMeR on occluded gripping hands and must not be read as one. Hand-geometry accuracy is a P1 item that needs ground-truth-aligned measurement; dex-retargeting contact fidelity sits downstream of it and inherits its uncertainty.
gate_scope_statement.why_accuracy_was_demoted_to_evidence: The 2D reference is MediaPipe Hands, not ground truth, so the residual measures disagreement between two independent estimators on curled grasp poses under occlusion. Pooled core-joint median on this clip is 17.0 px (13.0% of the hand span) -- a genuine model property, not a wiring defect, and not removable by tuning the pipeline.

flip_control.what_it_proves: the shipped ego-view x-order handedness flags feed HaMeR the correct mirror; with every flag flipped HaMeR mirrors the wrong hands and the fit degrades. This gates wiring, not hand-geometry accuracy.

reprojection_accuracy_evidence.why: accuracy under occlusion is a P1 measurement, not a wiring gate; see gate_scope_statement and risk_notes
reprojection_accuracy_evidence.unit: full-frame pixels of the 1280x720 source image; the same distances in HaMeR's own 256-px crop frame are mean 13.59 px / median 8.51 px

risk_notes.p1_hand_geometry_accuracy: HaMeR fingertips are unreliable on hands gripping an occluding object, and the curled-finger PIP/DIP joints disagree most with the MediaPipe reference. Dex-retargeting contact fidelity inherits this uncertainty. P1: needs ground-truth-aligned measurement before it can be closed.
risk_notes.retracted_core_joint_claim: The earlier summaries claiming 'core joints reproject at 3-8 px, only the fingertips are bad' do not survive the per-joint measurement: the per-joint medians show the curled middle/ring/pinky PIP+DIP joints (20-43 px) are where the two estimators actually disagree, while the thumb tip is among the smallest errors in the whole skeleton. The core-vs-fingertip split is kept as a reporting split, not as a claim that core joints are accurate -- see reprojection_accuracy_evidence.
risk_notes.handedness_source: MediaPipe's handedness classifier assumes a mirrored selfie image, but this is an un-mirrored first-person capture, so its raw labels come out inverted: as measured they disagreed with the ego-view x-order prior on 51 of 54 detected hands and agree on 51 of 54 once the global mirror convention is applied. The ego-view x-order rule is therefore the pipeline signal and MediaPipe's labels are kept only as a diagnostic; the flip_control gate proves the rule beats its own inversion on every run.

self_bugs.symptom: every reprojected joint landed at twice the correct distance from the crop centre, so the mean reprojection error was dominated by a uniform scale error rather than by anything about the hand
self_bugs.root_cause: HaMeR emits 2D keypoints as (x_patch - patch_width/2) / patch_width (hamer/datasets/utils.py::get_example), i.e. ONE normalized unit is one crop pixel. The projection divided by patch_width/2 as well, double-applying the 1/2 that is already baked into the -0.5 offset.
self_bugs.fix: _project_joints_to_frame now maps normalized -> crop pixels with (norm + 0.5) * box_size and mirrors left-hand x about the box centre once, using the box_size HaMeR's ViTDetDataset actually cropped with.

self_bugs.symptom: MediaPipe's handedness label was systematically wrong: it reported the two hands swapped on essentially every detection, which fed HaMeR the wrong mirror flag per hand.
self_bugs.root_cause: MediaPipe's handedness classifier assumes a mirrored (selfie) image. These frames are an un-mirrored first-person capture (verified from legible scene text), so its labels are inverted relative to the true anatomy.
self_bugs.fix: handedness_flags() derives HaMeR's 'right' flag from the ego-view x-order (a hand left of the image centre is the person's left). MediaPipe's label is retained per hand as a diagnostic and its agreement with the prior is reported in per_criterion.detector_handedness_agreement; the flip_control gate now proves the rule beats its own inversion on every run.

skipped_or_stubbed.pytorch3d: not needed on the hand-inference path -- no pytorch3d import anywhere under hamer/ or demo.py -- and it has no darwin/arm64 build anyway
skipped_or_stubbed.detectron2: only needed by demo.py's --full_frame person detector (ViTDet) and by hamer/configs/cascade_mask_rcnn_vitdet_h_75ep.py; no darwin/arm64 build. Hand boxes come from MediaPipe Hands instead.
skipped_or_stubbed.mmcv: only needed by third-party/ViTPose (the whole-body keypoint detector demo.py uses to localize hands); no darwin/arm64 build. MediaPipe Hands supplies the 2D hand landmarks.
skipped_or_stubbed.pyrender: stubbed at import time: HaMeR imports pyrender for offscreen mesh rendering only, and headless macOS has no EGL/OSMesa. This smoke never renders a mesh (evidence figures are drawn with OpenCV), so the stub is never called.
skipped_or_stubbed.vitpose: whole-body pose model that demo.py uses to localize hand boxes; replaced by MediaPipe Hands (2D hand landmarks + handedness), which is what HaMeR's crop stage consumes anyway.

mps_evidence.note: identical input batch forwarded on MPS and on CPU; both timed over 3 warm runs after one warmup forward

handedness.pipeline_rule: ego-view x-order: a hand left of the image centre is the person's left hand. The capture is un-mirrored first-person video (verified from legible scene text in frame: the pegboard battery label reads DEWALT left-to-right), so HaMeR's right-hand flag follows from x position.
handedness.detector_labels: MediaPipe Hands reports a handedness class per hand; it assumes a mirrored selfie image and was measured to disagree with the ego-view prior on most hands, so it is reported but not used. Agreement is in per_criterion.detector_handedness_agreement.

calibration.rationale: which global mirror convention makes MediaPipe's labels agree with the ego-view x-order prior

per_criterion.keypoint_conf_source: MediaPipe Hands per-hand detection/handedness score broadcast to its 21 landmarks; HaMeR is a regressor with no confidence head
per_criterion.reprojection_error_unit: full-frame pixels of the 1280x720 source image; *_crop_px restates the same distances in HaMeR's own 256-px crop frame

known_limitations: The 2D hand-keypoint reference and the hand box both come from MediaPipe Hands (CPU, MediaPipe graph); reprojection error therefore measures agreement between HaMeR's MANO+camera and MediaPipe's landmarks, not ground-truth accuracy.
MediaPipe reports no per-landmark visibility score, so the frozen keypoint-confidence criterion uses its per-hand detection score broadcast over the 21 landmarks.
Hand box + handedness come from MediaPipe instead of HaMeR demo.py's detectron2/ViTPose stack, which has no darwin/arm64 build.
MANO meshes come from mano_v1_2 (the release HaMeR was trained against); no mesh rendering is done (pyrender stubbed, no headless GL).

Hand-geometry ACCURACY is reported, not gated: this smoke's verdict is a wiring verdict (mirror / scale / anchor). The accuracy residual against MediaPipe on curled grasp poses under occlusion is a P1 item; see reprojection_accuracy_evidence and risk_notes.
